"''To Coruscant.''"
"''Coruscant? Uh, that doesn't compute. Uh, wait, uh, you're under arrest!|2163 and Qui-Gon Jinn|audio=2163-Jinn-Arrest-TPM.flac|}} '''2163''' was an [[OOM command battle droid]] that served within the [[Trade Federation Droid Army|Droid Army]] of the [[Trade Federation]] during its [[Invasion of Naboo|invasion]] of the [[planet]] [[Naboo]] in [[32 BBY]]. Following the [[Capture of Theed|occupation]] of the [[capital]] [[Theed]], 2163 and the [[droid]]s under its command were stationed in the [[Theed Hangar]] guarding the [[Naboo Royal Starship]] and various captive members of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces]]. When [[Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] entered the hangar with [[Monarch of Naboo|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] and her entourage, 2163 ordered them to halt and then declared that they were under [[Prisoner|arrest]] after Jinn stated he was taking the [[queen]] to the planet [[Coruscant]]. The [[Jedi]] then [[Death|destroyed]] 2163 with his [[Qui-Gon Jinn's lightsaber|lightsaber]]. ==Biography== ===Hangar guard=== {{Quote|There are too many of them.''"
"''That won't be a problem.|Quarsh Panaka and Qui-Gon Jinn discuss 2163 and the other droids in the hangar|audio=Panaka-Jinn-TooMany-TPM.flac|}} [[File:2163-Halt-TPM.png|thumb|right|300px|2163 attempted to stop Qui-Gon Jinn and his allies from leaving Naboo.]] 2163 was the designation of an [[OOM command battle droid]] that was manufactured by [[Baktoid Combat Automata]] for use in the [[Trade Federation Droid Army|Droid Army]] of the [[Trade Federation]]. The [[battle droid]] was part of the forces that the Federation deployed during their [[Invasion of Naboo|invasion]] of the [[planet]] [[Naboo]] in [[32 BBY]], and after the invaders [[Capture of Theed|occupied]] the world's [[capital]] [[city]], [[Theed]], he was stationed in the [[Theed Hangar]] used to store the [[Naboo Royal Starship]]. Various members of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces]] who had been captured during the invasion, including several [[pilot]]s of the [[Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps|Space Fighter Corps]], were held captive in the hangar, where they sat in a group on the floor surrounded by a circle of [[B1-series battle droid]]s under 2163's command. The unarmed [[OOM-series battle droid]] stood with four B1 [[droid]]s, including units [[1933]] and [[7169]], by the ramp leading up into the [[starship]], when [[Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his [[Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] led [[Monarch of Naboo|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] of Naboo and her entourage, including [[Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka]], the [[Gungan]] [[Jar Jar Binks]], her [[Naboo Royal Handmaidens|handmaidens]], and several [[Naboo Palace Guard]]s, into the hangar. ===Bisected=== {{Quote|Halt!''"
"''I am ambassador to the Supreme Chancellor. I'm taking these people to Coruscant.|2163 tries to stop Qui-Gon Jinn|audio=2163-Jinn-Halt-TPM.flac|}} [[File:2163-Death-TPM.png|thumb|left|250px|Qui-Gon Jinn caused enough doubt among the droids to get close to 2163 before bisecting the droid's torso with his lightsaber.]] Jinn walked steadily toward{{EncyclopediaCite|The Crisis on Naboo}} 2163 and the droids guarding the ship, causing a moment of doubt among them that allowed the Jedi to get into position before the command droid ordered Jinn to halt in front of him. The Jedi explained that he was an [[ambassador]] of [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum]] and that he was taking those with him to the planet [[Coruscant]], but this answer did not compute with the command droid, who ordered that Jinn and the others be placed under [[Prisoner|arrest]]. Before the droids around 2163 could even raise their [[E-5 blaster rifle|weapons]], the [[Jedi]] drew his [[Qui-Gon Jinn's lightsaber|lightsaber]] and destroyed the command droid, bisecting its torso and beheading the nearby 1933 in one sweep. Kenobi then freed the nearby captives and the pair destroyed the remaining droids in the hangar before making their escape with Amidala on board the Royal Starship. ==Characteristics== 2163 was an OOM-series battle droid with masculine programming that stood 1.91 [[meter]]s tall. He had [[bone]]-[[Color|white]] plating, black [[sensor]]s, and the yellow patterning shared by other command battle droids, as well as his designation imprinted on his back in [[Trade Federation Script]]. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|Why, you shall take them, then, to Coruscant. Alack, this doth Go 'gainst my programming, doth not compute! Behold, I place you all under arrest.''"
"''Thou shalt a ghost droid be ere I am through.|2163 and Qui-Gon Jinn's altered dialogue in ''[[William Shakespeare's The Phantom of Menace: Star Wars Part the First]]''|''[[William Shakespeare's The Phantom of Menace: Star Wars Part the First]]''}} [[File:PeterSerafinowicz.jpg|thumb|right|200px|2163 was voiced by Peter Serafinowicz.]] 2163 appeared in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], which was released on [[May 4]], [[1999]].''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]'' The droid's designation was not spoken in the film but was visible on its back. The command battle droid was voiced by [[Peter Serafinowicz]], the actor who also dubbed the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Maul|Darth Maul's]] voice in the film.{{InsiderCite|117|My Star Wars|My ''Star Wars'': Peter Serafinowicz}} In the film's script, 2163 is identified only as "Guard Droid" and "Droid Guard" and is only given the lines "Where are you going?" and "You're under arrest!". He is also described as drawing his weapon before being destroyed[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']] although he is visibly unarmed in the final cut of the film. In the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, [[2163/Legends|2163]] first appeared in the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]] of ''The Phantom Menace'' written by [[Terry Brooks]],[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]] which was released prior to the film on [[April 21]], 1999. ==Appearances== *{{Film|I}} {{1st}} ===Non-canon appearances=== *''[[William Shakespeare's The Phantom of Menace: Star Wars Part the First]]'' ==Sources== *{{SWE|technology|battledroid|battle droid}} *[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] {{Wreck}} *{{HelmetCollectionCite|54|Highlights of the Saga}} {{Imo}} *{{Databank|battle-droid|Battle Droid}} ==Notes and references== {{Mediacat|soundcat=Audio files of 2163|imagecat=Images of 2163}} {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |de=2163 }} [[Category:Droids of the Trade Federation]] [[Category:Droids with he/him pronouns]] [[Category:Droids with unspecified gender programming]] [[Category:OOM command battle droids]]
